transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-27 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Talia Nguyen (Redwood CSM), Ava Thompson (Crestfall Head of Security), Rakesh Menon (Crestfall Platform), Linda Cho (Compliance), Owen Price (DevOps)
---
Auto-summary (note: auto-generated, may be partial): Quick posture review; customer needs SOC2 artifacts and evidence access; want SSO and tight RBAC; ask about audit log retention and ability to export attestation-level logs for auditors; KMS question: can we bring keys or use Redwood-managed KMS?
---
00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. um we wanted to run through the security posture and make sure we can give your audit team what they need. quick rundawn of agenda — Trust Center, reports, RBAC/SSO, logs, KMS.
00:12 Ava Thompson: Thanks Jordan. we'll take notes. main ask up front — we have SOC2 audit next quarter and need to confirm evidence access and log exports, plus confirm that the ISO scope matches the hosted deployment.
00:25 Marco Ruiz: Cool, we can do that. quick question, are you planning to use Redwood hosted or Dedicated or Private? that changes how keys and data residency show up.
00:34 Rakesh Menon: We're evaluating hosted but must ensure EU data residency for prod. also our security team prefers customer-managed keys if possible.
00:42 Jordan Lee: Understood. Redwood supports both, we have Redwood-hosted with Trust Center docs and a Private option for VPC deployments. for KMS we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and envelope encryption.
00:58 Linda Cho: When you say "Trust Center" — will we be able to hand off the SOC2 Type II report to our auditors or only view it?
01:06 Jordan Lee: You'll get both. Trust Center provides downloadable reports for customers with the right role; we can also create auditor accounts with constrained access for the evidence portal.
01:15 Owen Price: What's the retention window for audit logs? our auditors ask for 12 months at a minimum and chain-of-custody info.
01:23 Marco Ruiz: Default is 90 days in the hosted plan, but for Dedicated/Private we can configure longer retention and export. we also export immutable logs and can sign them with HSM-backed keys if you need chain-of-custody.
01:40 Ava Thompson: Are those signed logs accessible as a batch export? or do we need to pull them via API?
01:45 Marco Ruiz: Both. we have a log export job that can produce SCV-like (CSV) and also a per-request API for incremental pulls. the signed bundle is generated per export and can be delivered to your S3 bucket in eu-west-1.
01:59 Rakesh Menon: okay that works. on RBAC/SSO — we use Okta and expect SAML. can you map to our groups and restrict Trust Center access to compliance only?
02:12 Jordan Lee: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for groups. RBAC is role-based mapped to SAML group claims; we can scope the Trust Center so only compliance and audit roles see reports.
02:24 Linda Cho: Do you support per-tenant key scoping for KMS? we don't want keys to be shared across customers.
02:30 Marco Ruiz: Absolutely. customer-managed KMS gives a per-customer key or envelope with your KMS. Redwood never stores your plaintext key. in hosted we can integrate with cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Google KMS) or if you go Private you can bring an HSM.
02:45 Owen Price: Any gotchas with cross-region keys? we want EU-only keys for EU prod.
02:50 Marco Ruiz: You'd provision the key in eu region and we'll reference it; there is a small latency penalty for remote KMS calls but it's typical. for strict residency we'd recommend a Private deployment in eu region.
03:05 Jordan Lee: Quick pause — any compliance controls you want to walk through specifically?
03:09 Ava Thompson: We'll need to map control IDs from our SOC2 matrix to Redwood controls, and ensure evidence paths exist for logging, change management, and access reviews.
03:20 Marco Ruiz: we maintain a controls mapping doc in the Trust Center — it lists Redwood controls, the associated evidence artifacts, and sample artifacts available for download. I'll show you that in a sec.
03:32 Jordan Lee: I'm going to share my screen — (screen share noise) — apologies if the screen share lags. (chuckle)
03:45 Jordan Lee: here is the Trust Center home page, top-right is 'Compliance artifacts' — you'll see SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 scope, encryption whitepaper, and the audit logs export panel.
03:58 Ava Thompson: I see it but some of the file names are truncated by the UI, is there a raw link to download the full report?
04:05 Jordan Lee: Yes, the artifact page has direct links — we'll send you the direct download link in the follow-up.
04:12 Linda Cho: Does the Trust Center include the control mapping CSV for automated ingestion into our GRC tool?
04:18 Marco Ruiz: We provide a controls CSV and a mapping doc. the CSV has control_id, description, artifact_reference, and typical sample evidence filename. it's a simple flat CSV you can ingest.
04:29 Rakesh Menon: For the evidence handoff — can we get a snapshot of logs for the review period that the SOC2 auditors will request?
04:36 Marco Ruiz: yes. we can run an evidence snapshot and deliver a signed archive to your S3. we'll need to coordinate the time window and the auditor's identity.
04:44 Jordan Lee: Note: for hosted customers we sometimes need an uplift for extended retention and signed exports — that is typically handled under a compliance add-on. we'll clarify pricing in the follow-up.
04:55 Ava Thompson: Pricing uplift is fine as long as we can meet residency and audit needs.
05:00 Owen Price: About RBAC — if we provision Okta groups and SCIM, how fast do permissions sync? we want near-real-time for offboarding cases.
05:10 Marco Ruiz: SCIM provisioning runs near real-time; changes are applied within a couple minutes. for immediate revocation we also support session revocation APIs to cut active tokens.
05:20 Linda Cho: Are audit logs showing user identity changes and who ran which operations in the console? we need that for access review evidence.
05:30 Marco Ruiz: yep, admin audit logs include actor, action, target, timestamp, and request_id. we also include the raw request payload for forensic purposes.
05:43 Rakesh Menon: On KMS — are you able to do envelope encryption with customer keys in AWS KMS and also have the secondary key in HSM?
05:52 Marco Ruiz: you can use envelope encryption where plaintext keys never leave your KMS. Redwood stores only the wrapped key material. for HSM-backed keys, if you choose Private deployment we can talk HSM-integration specifics.
06:05 Jordan Lee: I'm going to note down the next steps and owners. (typing)
06:10 Ava Thompson: Quick question on ISO 27001 — does your scope include cloud operations and SE team? our auditors require that evidence for patching and vulnerability mgmt includes those teams.
06:20 Marco Ruiz: Redwood's ISO scope includes hosting operations and development teams for the hosted product; the Trust Center lists the scope file. if you need an expanded scope for Private deployments, that is a separate engagement.
06:33 Linda Cho: For data residency, we need confirmation in writing that backups and logs for our EU org are stored only in EU regions.
06:41 Jordan Lee: We'll provide a residency statement for your account and a diagram of backup flows.
06:48 Rakesh Menon: Also need to confirm encryption at rest and in transit for exports — is TLS 1.2+ and AES-256 used?
06:55 Marco Ruiz: Yes TLS 1.2+ for transport, and AES-256-GCM for data at rest. signed archives are hashed with SHA-256 and optionally signed with an HSM key.
07:08 Ava Thompson: Good. what about evidence access for auditors — do you create temporary auditor accounts or do you prefer we give our auditors S3 access?
07:16 Jordan Lee: Both options supported. auditor accounts in Trust Center are easiest — we can limit scope and TTL. S3 delivery is also possible if auditors prefer direct access to exported artifacts.
07:28 Owen Price: For the demo — can you run a quick KMS envelope wrap/unwarp example so we can show auditors the chain?
07:34 Marco Ruiz: yes I can demo a small export. i can show key reference to your KMS, the wrapped key blob, and how Redwood references it. we can redact names for the demo.
07:44 Linda Cho: Will that demo include the signed hash so we can validate chain-of-custody?
07:48 Marco Ruiz: yes, the export will include a signature file and manifest.
07:55 Jordan Lee: Great. a few admin items — we'll add 'Trust Center access' deliverable, 'RBAC mapping work' and a 'KMS demo and log export' to next steps.
08:05 Ava Thompson: Sounds good. timeline — we need SOC2 artifacts by Aug 29 for prep, and want the demo the first week of September.
08:14 Jordan Lee: We'll aim for that. Marco, can you take point on the technical deliverables?
08:18 Marco Ruiz: Yep, i'll own the KMS demo and the log export.
08:21 Talia Nguyen: I'll coordinate access provisioning and will send the Trust Center invite to the list Jordan shares.
08:27 Jordan Lee: Perfect. Any final questions before we wrap?
08:31 Rakesh Menon: one more — are there any known limitations in your audit artifacts for MFA and SSO session logs? our auditors want session MFA events.
08:40 Marco Ruiz: we do capture MFA events as part of authentication logs and include them in admin audit exports; if you need higher fidelity we can enable extended auth logging for the account.
08:50 Ava Thompson: ok that covers it. thanks everyone.
08:55 Jordan Lee: Thanks all — we'll follow up with links and schedule the demo.
09:00 (call ends)
